# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41)

## Problem statement

After the End of Turn phase animations finish, the player currently gets only a
one-line instruction text (`Income: +N coins | Incident: <name>`, via
`closingSummary`) and the next day starts automatically. There is no moment to
understand what happened that turn — how much income came in and from where,
what was spent (ongoing costs), one-off events, and each player's standing.
This item adds a **Turn Summary dialog** that appears once all End of Turn
animations have completed, showing the current state of the game (businesses
owned per player, this turn's income and expenses, one-off income/expenses from
events, and other useful state), with a **[ Next Turn ]** button to continue
and a **[ Bank Loan ]** button (disabled until MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands).

## Users

- **Main Street single-player player** — after each turn's closing
  animations, wants a readable summary of what just happened and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action instead of an auto-advance.
- **Main Street competitive player** — unchanged for now (see Constraints:
  competitive is deliberately out of scope in this item).

**User stories:**

- As a player, when my turn's income/incident animations finish, I see a dialog
  summarising the turn (income by phase, expenses by category, one-off event
  deltas, net change, businesses owned) so I can learn from each turn.
- As a player, I can click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next week — the day
  does not advance until I do.
- As a player, I see a **[ Bank Loan ]** affordance that is visibly
  unavailable until the loans feature exists, so I know the option is planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In normal single-player play (deferred/closing path), after all End of Turn animations (phased income show + incident reveal) complete, a Turn Summary dialog appears and the next day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**; reduced-motion, tutorial and replay modes skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog reports, for the turn just closed: businesses owned, income subtotals per phase (base / synergy / reputation / events), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), incident and one-off event deltas, net coin / reputation / score change, and closing coin / reputation / score values; the ledger is owner-keyed (ready for per-player rows), but the panel renders the single (human) seat because the competitive dialog is deferred (see Constraint: competitive out of scope).
3. The dialog's **[ Bank Loan ]** button is always rendered **disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind a single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans) will replace; it is never shown enabled by this item.
4. The dialog is NOT presented in competitive mode (operator decision) — existing per-seat closing text (`perSeatClosingSummary`) is unchanged.
5. A Phaser-free model (`MainStreetTurnSummary`, mirroring `MainStreetGameOverSummary`) renders the dialog content from committed engine data; the engine's `TurnResult` is extended with an end-of-turn ledger (expense subtotals, per-phase income subtotals, one-off deltas, net change) so every value shown is testable without a browser.
6. At least one automated test per surfaced value (model tests, engine ledger tests, and a dialog overlay test); **all related documentation is updated** (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` end-of-turn section, plus any references in README/dev docs); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground`
  + `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`; all elements parented into
  `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201; everything pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance (reduced-motion safe);
  button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- The dialog is presentation-only: it reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In the deferred path the turn's
  deltas land exactly once (idempotent `endOfTurnDeltasApplied` guard) before

# `implement.py phase_start` records the worktree as `repo_root` on resume-from-worktree

discovered-from:MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP

## Problem statement

`phase_start` resolves the main checkout root correctly at Step 6.5
(`repo_root = _get_repo_root() or ...`) but then **recomputes it from
`Path.cwd()` at Step 8** and writes that value into
`.implement_state.json`. When `start` is run as a resume from inside an
existing worktree — the normal driven-child pattern — `cwd` *is* the
worktree, so the state file records the worktree as `repo_root` and every
downstream consumer of that value is wrong: `phase_finish` cannot fast-forward
`dev` in the main checkout, and its worktree-removal gate refuses to remove
"the repository root", so a successfully pushed implementation is left
stranded with the work item reset to `open`.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer** resuming a driven child session or re-running `start`
  in an existing worktree: needs `start` → `finish` to work unchanged, with no
  manual state-file surgery.
- **Parent/phase session** orchestrating children: a stranded child leaves the
  parent phase unable to close the epic and burns a session on recovery.
- **Maintainer** reading `.implement_state.json`: needs `repo_root` to mean one
  thing — the main checkout — so state is diagnosable.

Example user stories:

> As a driven child session resuming its worktree, I want `implement.py start`
> to record the main checkout root, so that `finish` can fast-forward `dev`
> and remove my worktree.

> As a parent session, I want a child that already has a bad state file to
> still finish cleanly, so that I do not have to hand-edit JSON to unblock an
> epic.

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (source repo `SorraAgents`; the global
install `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`):

| Line (at `91de33cf5`) | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 4110 | `repo_root = _get_repo_root() or str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | Step 6.5 — correct main-root resolution (used for the parent-branch refresh) |
| 4178 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | **Defect** — Step 8 overwrites the correct value before `_store_signal_globals` / `write_state` |
| 4613-4616 | `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else (...)` | `phase_finish` trusts the (wrong) state value for the `dev` fast-forward, the push and `_sync_parent_branch` |
| 4732 | `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root if state else None)` | Gate 1 compares `worktree_path.resolve()` with `repo_root.resolve()` → `RuntimeError: REFUSE to remove the repository root` |
| 4872 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | `phase_abort` Step 3 — same defect class: `_restore_repo_state` runs `git checkout dev` / `git pull` in the worktree, both silently failing (`check=False`) |

Failure sequence observed (resume-from-worktree start):

1. `start` writes `repo_root = <worktree>`; `_store_signal_globals` gets the
   same value, so the SIGTERM handler's `_restore_repo_state` would also run in
   the worktree.
2. `finish` Step 5 tries `git checkout dev` inside the worktree → fails ("already
   checked out"); caught and logged as a warning, so the main checkout is never
   fast-forwarded (the pre-push context-budget gate then works from a stale
   checkout).
3. `finish` Step 6 pushes successfully from the worktree, **then** Step 7 calls
   `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=<worktree>)`, which raises the
   safety-gate `RuntimeError`; the outer handler resets the item to `open`,
   posts no completion comment, and leaves the worktree in place.
4. The worktree can then be removed by a later cleanup pass (signal handler /
   parent phase) **while the child session's `cwd` is still inside it** — the
   reported end state: a session stranded on a deleted working directory.
   `_remove_worktree` deliberately `chdir`s to `repo_root` before removal, but
   with the wrong `repo_root` stored it either raises before that `chdir` or
   chdirs into the worktree it is about to delete.

Live evidence of the same defect (recorded during this intake, not fixed here):

```
.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite/.implement_state.json
  "repo_root": ".../.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite"
  "started_at": "2026-10-24T11:11:45Z"
```

(SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite — is still
`open`/`intake_complete`; that worktree is the recovery target, not scope of
this item.)

## Desired change

1. **Fix the source of truth.** Make Step 8 use the already-resolved main
   checkout root (reuse the Step 6.5 value / call `_get_repo_root()`), so
   `_store_signal_globals` and the state file always carry the main checkout,
   never the worktree.
2. **Repair stale state defensively.** In `phase_finish` and `phase_abort`,
   treat a `state.repo_root` that resolves to the worktree itself (or to a path
   inside it) as stale and fall back to `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)`; keep
   the correct value for the remaining steps (and, optionally, rewrite the
   state file). This is what unblocks worktrees already stranded by the bug
   **without** hand-editing JSON.
3. **Fix the abort path.** `phase_abort` Step 3 must restore the *main*
   checkout when invoked from inside the worktree.
4. **Regress-proof it.** A test that fails on the pre-fix code: a real
   temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, `cwd` set inside the worktree,
   `start` resumed, asserting the persisted `repo_root` is the main root; plus a
   finish-gate assertion that the worktree path is never handed to
   `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`.

## Implementation plan (test-first)

Ordered so the regression test lands **first** and is proven to fail before
the fix (test-first ordering per the implement skill):

1. **Test (red).** New `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py`
   using a real `tmp_path` git repo (`git init`, one commit on `dev`) plus a
   linked worktree (`git worktree add`), with no `_get_repo_root` mocking:
   - `cwd` inside the worktree, `phase_start` resumed → `.implement_state.json`
     `repo_root` is the main checkout root and the value handed to
     `_store_signal_globals` matches it;
   - a state file whose `repo_root` is the worktree itself → `phase_finish`'s
     worktree-removal gate succeeds and the worktree path is never passed to
     `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`;
   - `phase_abort` run from inside the worktree leaves the **main** checkout on
     the parent branch (and behaves identically when run from the main
     checkout).
   Confirm all three fail against the pre-fix code, then keep them passing.
2. **Fix Step 8.** Reuse the already-resolved Step 6.5 `repo_root`
   (`_get_repo_root()`), removing the `Path.cwd()` recomputation, so
   `_store_signal_globals` and `write_state` always carry the main checkout.
3. **Harden `phase_finish`.** Treat a `state.repo_root` equal to, or inside,
   `worktree_path` as stale: log the rejected and derived values at WARNING
   and derive the main root with `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (falling back
   to discovery), then use it for the `dev` fast-forward, the push,
   `_sync_parent_branch` and the `_remove_worktree` call.
   `_remove_worktree`'s own gates stay untouched.
4. **Fix `phase_abort` Step 3.** Apply the same stale-state rejection, then
   `_restore_repo_state(main_root)` so `git checkout`/`pull` run in the main
   checkout instead of silently failing inside the worktree.
5. **Docs.** State-file schema note — `repo_root` is always the **main
   checkout** — in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, plus code comments at each corrected
   site.
6. **Verify.** Changed-scope test run then full suite via `/skill:test`;
   commit → push on the SorraAgents `dev` branch (this repo only).

Between steps: re-read the next step's description before starting it; if a
step reveals a further `Path.cwd()`-derived repo root, file it as a linked
work item rather than widening this fix (see Risks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a fresh `start` **and** a resume-from-worktree `start` (cwd inside
      `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-…`), the written `.implement_state.json`
      records `repo_root` as the main checkout root (`git rev-parse
      --git-common-dir`'s parent), never the worktree path; the same value is
      passed to `_store_signal_globals`.
- [ ] `phase_finish` treats a stale `state.repo_root` equal to (or inside) the
      worktree as invalid and derives the main root from the worktree, so the
      worktree-removal gate succeeds instead of raising `REFUSE to remove the
      repository root`.
- [ ] `phase_abort` run from inside a worktree restores the **main** checkout
      (`git checkout <parent-branch>` / pull), not the worktree.
- [ ] A regression test in `skill/implement/tests/` reproduces the
      resume-from-worktree start against a real temporary git repo and linked
      worktree (no `_get_repo_root` mocking), and **fails on the pre-fix code**
      while passing after the fix; a second assertion covers the stale-state
      finish path.
- [ ] `_remove_worktree`'s safety gates are unchanged in behaviour: removing
      the true main checkout is still refused (existing coverage retained), and
      the fix supplies the correct root rather than relaxing the check.
- [ ] All existing `skill/implement/tests/` tests pass via the project test
      skill, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
      where they describe `repo_root`, and any relevant wiki or docs site
      entries (state file schema note: `repo_root` is always the main checkout).

## Constraints

- The fix lives in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in the **SorraAgents**
  framework repo (the global install is a symlink), while this work item lives
  in the MainStreet worklog. Implementation therefore runs from the SorraAgents
  checkout with the `MS-…` id; `wl` resolves the MainStreet store by
  prefix-to-sibling scan, and the commit lands on SorraAgents `dev`. Do **not**
  copy `implement.py` into this repo.
- No behavioural change beyond repo-root resolution: commit → push → worktree
  removal ordering, the test/refactor gates and the state-file schema stay as
  they are (only the value written changes).
- No hand editing of live `.implement_state.json` files and no deletion of
  existing stranded worktrees as part of this item.
- The worktree-removal safety gate must keep refusing the real main checkout —
  do not weaken it to make the symptom disappear.
- Keep the change small and local: no refactor of `_get_repo_root`, no new
  abstraction over phase plumbing.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the four call sites, named
  durably (line numbers drift; prefer the anchors): `phase_start` Step 8
  `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` (the defect), `phase_finish`
  Step 5 `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else ...`, the
  `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root if state else None)`
  call in `phase_finish` Step 7, and `phase_abort` Step 3's
  `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` before `_restore_repo_state`.
  Reference implementations to reuse: `_get_repo_root` (git-common-dir
  resolution), `_remove_worktree` (already falls back to `_get_repo_root()`
  when `repo_root` is `None`), `_store_signal_globals`, `_restore_repo_state`.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — New regression test module (real temp git repo +
  linked worktree); existing `test_phase_start_claim.py` mocks
  `_get_repo_root`, which is exactly why this defect escaped.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Document the `repo_root` invariant if the
  worktree/state wording implies cwd derivation.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — State-file / repo-root resolution
  guidance, including the resume-from-worktree case.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Read-only reference: this is the
  `_get_repo_root`-equivalent module used elsewhere; confirm no duplicated
  cwd-derived root logic needs the same fix.

## Related work

- MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP — Export end-of-turn income-collection cap constant
  (completed): the driven-child session during which the state file was written
  with the wrong `repo_root`; that session then died of provider exhaustion.
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — MainStreetScene browser-test load tolerance (parent,
  unrelated topic; this item was filed from one of its driven sessions).
- MS-0MV59PJM5008VBLW — `implement.py` non-fast-forward push recovery
  references undefined `cwd` (completed): precedent for an `implement.py`
  phase_finish defect tracked in this worklog while the fix lands in the
  framework repo.
- WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 / WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M — earlier `implement.py`
  finish/push recovery fixes (framework repo commits `6229a0605`, `a99a6b848`).
- SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite: live item
  whose state file currently carries the worktree as `repo_root` (recovery
  target once this fix lands; not scope here).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_remove_worktree` (safety gate 1),
  `_get_repo_root` (git-common-dir resolution), `_discover_worktree`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the resume-from-worktree path is the only way to write a bad
  `repo_root`; a fresh start from the main checkout writes the right value
  (verified against existing state files in both repos). Any other cwd-derived
  site would show up as the same symptom, hence the abort-path fix.
- **Risk:** a stale-state fallback in `phase_finish` could mask a genuinely
  mis-specified `repo_root` (e.g. an operator-pointed state file). Mitigation:
  log at WARNING which value was rejected and which was derived, and keep the
  `_remove_worktree` gate independent of the fallback.
- **Risk:** the regression test needs a real linked worktree, which is slower
  and can be flaky on odd hosts. Mitigation: one small module, no browser, no
  test-suite invocation inside it; create the repo and worktree in `tmp_path`
  and assert exit codes/paths only.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is auditing every `Path.cwd()`
  repo-root derivation across all skills (audit, ship, test, report). That is
  out of scope here — record any further sites found as linked work items.
- **Risk:** the monorepo `core/` engine-sync workflow does not apply (this is
  the framework repo, not MainStreet `core/`); confirm no `engine:sync` step is
  needed before implementing.
- **Risk:** fixing the abort path changes `_restore_repo_state`'s behaviour when
  aborting from the main checkout (it should be identical) — assert this in the
  same test module.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking questions were needed: the filed description already contains the
root cause, the failing call site and the observed symptom, and the remaining
choices were resolved from repository evidence.

- Q: Which repository carries the fix, given the item lives in the MainStreet
  worklog? — Answer (agent, from repo evidence — producer may override): the
  SorraAgents framework repo (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`);
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, and
  `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` documents prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution so
  an `MS-…` id resolves from the framework checkout. Precedent:
  MS-0MV59PJM5008VBLW. Source: `readlink -f ~/.pi/agent/skills`,
  `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` §"Worklog-dir resolution for skill scripts".
- Q: Scope — fix only Step 8, or also the finish/abort consumers? — Answer
  (agent, documented assumption — producer may override): fix Step 8 (root
  cause) **and** harden `phase_finish` against stale state **and** fix
  `phase_abort` Step 3 (same defect class, one line each), because a live
  worktree (SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK) already carries the bad value and would
  otherwise need hand-edited JSON. Source: `.implement_state.json` inspection
  of `.worklog/worktrees/*`.
- Q: Priority — is `low` right for a bug that strands sessions? — Answer
  (agent classification — producer may override): `medium`; it breaks the
  implement workflow on resume and leaves live bad state, but it is neither a
  security/data-loss issue nor a broken build. Source: priority classification

- Q: Should this item stay a child of the browser-wait epic
  (MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ)? — Answer (agent, documented assumption — producer may
  override): left unchanged to avoid unrelated worklog graph edits; the link is
  historical (filed from one of that epic's driven sessions) and noted in
  Related work. Source: `wl show MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4 --children --json`.
- Q: Duplicate check — is this already fixed elsewhere? — Answer (agent
  research): no. `wl search "repo_root phase_start worktree"` and
  `wl search "implement.py repo_root"` return only this item; the nearest
  siblings are the completed `implement.py` push/cwd fixes, which address
  different lines. Source: `wl search` output, `git log` on
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.

### Plan session (agent, `/skill:plan` — 2026-10-25)

No producer interview was required: the filed brief already carries the root
cause, the failing call sites, a four-point desired change and seven testable
ACs, so the plan skill ran the automated review stages over the existing
content instead of decomposing a single-file bug fix into child items.

- Q: Is decomposition into child work items warranted? — Answer (agent, from
  the pre-check + Step 1 heuristics): no. Effort `Small`, risk `Medium`, one

  Decision recorded via `apply_coverage_review` (no children → coverage
  trivially complete). Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`, existing
  children = none.

# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.

# Release derived-files step commits a spurious core submodule bump, breaking the engine pin contract

**Headline:** Restrict the ship skill's derived-files regeneration commit so it can never stage submodule pointer changes, and prove it with regression tests on a submodule fixture — fixing the spurious `core` gitlink bump that broke the v0.1.22 release pin contract.

## Problem statement

The ship skill's dev→main release runs the consumer repo's `npm run build` on the merged tree and commits the regenerated **tracked** files (`Regenerate derived version files for v<version>`, via `skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` + `git add -u`). Because `core` is a git submodule whose pointer the build can move — main-street's `npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances `./core` to the engine remote tip — `git add -u` also stages the gitlink. The release commit then silently bumps the submodule pointer while `configs/engine-pin.json` stays unchanged, and the release pin-contract gate (`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` "release pin contract (AC3)") fails on the merged tree, blocking the release with a misleading pin-drift error. Observed in the v0.1.22 release attempt (commit `155eead1`: `core` → `9ee194e0`, pin left at `d907af9f`).

## Users

- **Release operator (maintainer)** — runs `/skill:ship release` and expects a deterministic, reproducibly built main tree. User story: "As a release operator, I want the derived-files commit to contain only regenerated tracked files, so a stray submodule checkout in my working tree can never silently change what gets shipped or trip the pin-contract gate."
- **Game developer (internal)** — runs `npm run build` with the dev auto-sync (`engine:sync`) enabled and should never worry that a local engine advance leaks into a release. User story: "As a game developer, I want my dev-submodule hygiene to be irrelevant to releases, so I never have to `git submodule update --init core` before a colleague ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The derived-files regeneration step never stages submodule pointer changes: after staging tracked modifications, all staged submodule pointers (mode `160000` entries) are unstaged generically — no `core`-specific hardcoding and no per-repo allow-list — so a derived-files commit can never contain a gitlink bump. (Fix lands in SorraAgents under SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ.)
- A regression test in **both** test copies (`SorraAgents/tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs`, authoritative/CI, and `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs`, skill-local) uses a local-path submodule fixture (`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`): a submodule checkout whose HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink must not end up in the derived-files commit, and when the gitlink is the *only* change no commit is made.
- Existing regeneration behaviour is preserved (guard rails): no `build` script → no-op; successful build commits the regenerated tracked derived files; failing build is non-fatal with a warning.
- The fix is verified against the pin contract: on a merged tree where the only drift is a worktree `core` at an unpinned SHA, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` "release pin contract (AC3)" passes (pin equals the committed gitlink), and the framework's node test suite is green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: `docs/dev/release-process.md` and `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) state that submodule pointers are excluded from the derived-files commit; any code comments in `regenerate-version.js` describe the gitlink exclusion.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (main-street suite green on `dev`; SorraAgents node suite green).

## Constraints

- **Implementation home:** the code change, tests and docs land in the **SorraAgents** repo (agent-framework; `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship` is a symlink to its `skill/ship`), under companion item **SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ**. This item (MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57) is **Blocked-by** that item and closes when the SA work lands and the pin contract is re-verified.
- **Generic, not repo-specific:** the failure occurs in the generic `regenerate-version.js` consumer-repo helper; the fix must work for any submodule, not only `core`. Rejected in intake: pathspec exclusion of `core` (option B) and per-repo allow-lists (option C).
- **No engine design changes:** the `engine:sync`/`engine:verify` split and pin ownership (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED) stay as-is; `build:release` (`engine:verify`) is not wired into the generic regeneration step (option E rejected).
- **Release flow ordering unchanged:** the derived-files step stays post-merge, pre-tag, non-fatal — only its staging behaviour changes.
- **No main-street source edits for the fix itself**; main-street's role is verification (pin-contract test + suite) and docs, plus this work item's bookkeeping.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` (SorraAgents): reads `scripts.build`, runs `npm run build`, stages with `git add -u`, commits with subject `Regenerate derived version files for v<version>`; also exposes `regenerateDerivedFiles()` for tests with an injected `runBuild`.
- Tests: `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` (skill-local mirror) and `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` (authoritative; CI). Three paths covered: no build script (no-op), successful regeneration + commit, failing build (non-fatal). No submodule coverage today.
- main-street: `.gitmodules` maps `core` → `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git` (branch `dev`); `package.json` `build = "npm run engine:sync && tsc --noEmit && vite build"` (advances `./core`); `configs/engine-pin.json` holds `{"sha": "…"}` written by the release process; `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` asserts the committed gitlink equals the pin.
- Observed failure: v0.1.22 (runs 2026-10-24T22:57Z, 2026-10-25T00:36Z) — release commit bumped `core` to `9ee194e0` while the pin stayed `d907af9f`; workaround was bumping the pin on `dev` (commit `13e7283b`) so pointer == pin == tip.

## Desired change

- In `regenerateDerivedFiles`, after `git add -u` (and before diffing/committing), unstage every staged submodule pointer: derive staged entries whose index mode is `160000` (gitlink) and run `git reset`/`git restore --staged` on exactly those paths (scope: `<mode> 160000` entries only, so unrelated staged changes are untouched).
- Add the submodule regression matrix to both test files (local-path submodule fixture mirroring main-street's engine-sync tests): (a) advanced-submodule checkout + a regenerated tracked file → commit contains the tracked file only, gitlink unchanged; (b) advanced-submodule checkout with no other changes → no commit; (c) dirty working tree in the submodule → still no gitlink staging.
- Update SorraAgents docs (`docs/dev/release-process.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`) and the script's header comment to state that submodule pointers are excluded from the derived-files commit.
- In main-street, re-run the release flow verification (or equivalent dry-run on a merged tree with a drifted `core` checkout) to confirm the pin-contract gate passes; record evidence on the work item.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` (SorraAgents) — gitlink exclusion after `git add -u`; header comment update.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` (SorraAgents) — skill-local regression tests with submodule fixture.
- `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` (SorraAgents) — authoritative/CI regression tests with submodule fixture.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` + `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — document the exclusion.
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` (main-street) — unchanged; the pin-contract test that failed and now serves as verification.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` (main-street) — unchanged by this fix; must stay in sync with the committed gitlink.

## Related work

# Make the composed engine explicit: fail loudly when a worktree's `./core` is stale

**Headline:** Every in-repo test invocation currently composes whatever `./core` happens to be checked out (worktrees keep the gitlink they were created from, silently behind the engine pin), so a green run can hide engine regressions. Add a fast, offline preflight to the test entry path that names the composed engine SHA and fails loudly when `./core` is behind (or diverged from) `configs/engine-pin.json`, then document the composition matrix.

## Problem statement

`npm test`, the changed-scope `npx vitest run <files>` gate and the dev-push browser gate all compose the `./core` submodule exactly as checked out; nothing in the test path verifies *which* engine that is. Worktrees created by `implement.py` only run `git submodule update --init --recursive`, which checks out the gitlink recorded by the commit the worktree was branched from — a commit that silently predates the engine pin. Observed in this repo: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT-*/core` at `e4d0e10b` (`v0.1.21-6`) and `.worklog/worktrees/f7-competitive-before-85d23dbb/core` at `8c602332` (`v0.1.20-39`), both behind the pinned `9ee194e0` and the `1c9900a1` dev tip. Only `npm run build` / `build:electron` (via `engine:sync`) advance a worktree's `core`.

## Users

- **Implement agent — user story:** "As an implement agent working in a fresh worktree, I need my first test run to tell me the engine it composed is stale and how to fix it, instead of returning a green suite that never saw the pinned engine code."
- **Release/producer — user story:** "As a producer reviewing a green suite, I need each run to record the engine SHA it composed, so a green result is evidence about a known engine, not an anonymous one."
- **Maintainer — user story:** "As a maintainer I need the composition matrix (test run vs build vs release verify vs fresh worktree) written down in one place, so 'which engine did this test?' has a single documented answer."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Offline preflight on the test path.** A fast (target < 1 s), network-free preflight runs for every Vitest invocation in this repo — `npm test`, changed-scope `npx vitest run <files>` and `npx vitest run --project browser` — and fails the run loudly, naming the composed SHA, the pin SHA and the remediation, when `./core` is **not** the pin and **not** a descendant of the pin (behind or diverged), when the pin commit is absent from the local `./core` clone, or when `./core` is uninitialised/empty. A dirty `./core` is reported loudly but does not fail (composition is still identifiable). Deliberate bypass is `ENGINE_CHECKOUT_CHECK=warn|off`, logged every time it is used. The wiring is a documented local surgical addition to `vite.config.ts` (that file is auto-generated from the engine-owned `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) and is held in place by a drift-guard test, so a re-scaffold cannot silently drop the gate. Verified by unit tests over temp-git fixtures plus a manual stale-worktree reproduction.
- **AC2 — The composed engine is explicit.** A passing preflight records the composed engine identity (short SHA plus `git describe` tag when available) alongside the pin, so any green suite states which engine it composed — at most one identical line per process, even when several Vitest projects (each `extends: true`) trigger the global setup, and verified by a unit test asserting the rendered line through an injected logger.
- **AC3 — Composition matrix documented.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` gains a composition matrix covering: `npm test` / changed-scope / dev-push browser gate → checkout present, preflight must accept it (pin or descendant); `npm run build` / `build:electron` → dev head after `engine:sync`; `npm run build:release` → detached at the pin after `engine:verify`; a freshly created worktree → whatever gitlink its branch recorded, until `engine:sync` runs. `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the preflight in the `npm test` pipeline, and README/DEPLOYMENT note it where they describe the submodule and the test command. Code comments in the new module state the rules and their rationale.
- **AC4 — Existing engine contract tests stay green.** `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` (dirty guard, pin mismatch, release pin contract) still passes unchanged, and the new preflight tests cover: pin → pass, ahead-of-pin (post-`engine:sync` dev head) → pass, behind pin → fail with remediation, pin commit missing locally → fail, uninitialised `core` → fail, documented bypass env var → warning path.
- **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** The VitePress site under `docs/` is generated from these Markdown pages, so updating them updates the published site; no separate docs-site entry exists or is required.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **In-repo scope only.** `implement.py` (worktree creation, the framework's `_ensure_submodules`) lives in SorraAgents, and `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` is engine-owned and must never be hand-edited from here. The refresh-at-worktree-creation half of the original AC is therefore out of scope for this repo and is recorded as a follow-up (see Risks); this item delivers the *fails-loudly* half, which is entirely in-repo.
- **Offline by default.** The preflight must not fetch, not contact the remote, and not depend on a cached `origin/dev` ref: worktrees routinely have stale refs and airgapped runs must still gate. Reachability from the pin is therefore decided from the local commit graph (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), not from the branch tip.
- **Fast and fail-fast.** The check must be cheap enough to sit in front of every Vitest run, including the changed-scope gate, which runs per test file group.
- **No CI beyond the npm builds** (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED) — the test path *is* the gate, so the check must live there, not in a workflow file.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `"test": "tsx scripts/run-tests.ts --timeout-ms 720000 --project unit --project unit-cli"`, `"pretest": "tsx src/scripts/check-playwright-chromium.ts"`, `"build": "npm run engine:sync && tsc --noEmit && vite build"`, `"engine:sync"`/`"engine:verify"` wrap `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`.
- `vite.config.ts` defines three Vitest projects (`unit-cli`, `unit`, `browser`) at the root config; there is **no** `globalSetup` today, so a config-level setup is the one place that covers every invocation, including direct `npx vitest run` calls. It is **auto-generated** by the engine-owned `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, so the accepted pattern for local changes is a documented "LOCAL SURGICAL ADDITION" header comment plus a drift-guard test (existing precedents: `CLI_TEST_FILES` / `unit-cli`, the `sequence.groupOrder` split, `projectCoverageReporter` — guarded by `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/testing-docs-projects.test.ts`).
- Precedent for the pattern: `src/scripts/check-playwright-chromium.ts` is a sub-second, network-free `pretest` pre-check with injectable dependencies and printed remediation (MS-0MVJPV0BV000LSLW), documented in `docs/dev/testing.md` § "npm test".
- Fixture precedent: `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` builds network-free temp git repos (`makeGame()`: engine repo on `dev` + game repo with a `core` submodule and a pin file) via `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`.
- Current repo state (evidence): pin `9ee194e0`, committed gitlink `9ee194e0`, `origin/dev` cached ref `1c9900a1` (pin is an ancestor, 2 commits behind), six worktree `core` checkouts behind at `09723c4b`/`7e43108c`/`e4d0e10b`/`8c602332`.

## Desired change

1. **New preflight module** (e.g. `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`) exporting a pure `checkEngineCheckout({ repoRoot, env, deps })` that returns `{ ok, composedSha, pinSha, describe, reason, message }`. Rules: pass when `HEAD === pin` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pin> <HEAD>`; fail when behind/diverged, when `<pin>` is not present in the local `core` clone, or when `core` has no `HEAD`; warn (not fail) on a dirty `core`. Bypass via `ENGINE_CHECKOUT_CHECK=warn|off` (logged every time it is used).
2. **Wire it once, for every project**: register it as Vitest's `globalSetup` in the root `test` config so `npm test`, the changed-scope gate and browser runs all pass through it, and expose it as `npm run engine:check` for manual/CI use. (Alternative wiring — a second `pretest` command — covers only `npm test`; the config-level setup is preferred because the changed-scope gate invokes Vitest directly.)
3. **Tests** (offline, temp-git fixtures in the style of `engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`): pin pass, ahead-of-pin pass, behind fail, missing-pin-object fail, uninitialised `core` fail, bypass env var behaviour, and the message text carrying both SHAs plus the `npm run engine:sync` remediation.
4. **Docs**: composition matrix in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`; preflight description in `docs/dev/testing.md`; short notes in `README.md` (submodule/checkout section) and `DEPLOYMENT.md` (test/build commands).

**Order of work (test-first):** write the offline fixture tests (item 3) against the agreed contract *first*, then the
preflight module (item 1), then the wiring plus its drift guard (item 2), then the docs (item 4). Keep
`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` green throughout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts` — New: pure checker plus the Vitest `globalSetup` entry point.
- `tests/main-street/engine-checkout-precheck.test.ts` — New: offline fixture tests for every pass/fail branch (AC1/AC4).
- `tests/main-street/vite-config-engine-check-guard.test.ts` — New: drift guard (precedent `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts`, `testing-docs-projects.test.ts`) asserting `vite.config.ts` still registers the precheck as root `test.globalSetup` and `package.json` still exposes `engine:check`, so an engine re-scaffold cannot silently drop the gate (AC1).
- `vite.config.ts` — Wire `test.globalSetup` to the precheck so every project and every direct Vitest run is gated.
- `package.json` — Add `engine:check` script (manual invocation, same code path); keep `pretest` unchanged.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — New "Composition matrix" section: which engine each invocation composes and which gate applies.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — Document the preflight in the `npm test` pipeline and the changed-scope caveat.
- `README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — Point at the preflight where the submodule and the test/build commands are described.
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — Unchanged, but must stay green (regression guard on the pin contract).

**Reuse (do not re-implement):** `readPin` and `submoduleIsDirty` are already exported by the engine-owned
`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (import via the `@core-scripts/engine-sync.mjs` alias, as
`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` does). The precheck should consume those rather than re-parse
`configs/engine-pin.json` or re-run `git status`. **Do not edit** `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` or
`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — both are engine-owned (repo boundary rule).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — acceptance window.** "Pin or descendant of the pin" is chosen over "pin only" and over "reachable from `origin/dev`": a descendant contains the pinned engine, so the stale-engine hazard is gone, while an unrefreshed `origin/dev` ref cannot produce a false failure. A pin-only rule would reject the post-`npm run build` checkout that the dev workflow deliberately creates.
- **Assumption — scope of the fix.** The refresh-at-worktree-creation option is out of this repo's boundary (framework + engine-owned scripts); the fails-loudly option satisfies the same AC user-visibly and is fully testable here. Follow-up (not filed by this item): have `implement.py`'s `_ensure_submodules` run `engine:sync` (network-tolerant, best-effort) so worktrees start current.
- **Risk — first-run friction.** Agents in existing stale worktrees will now fail every test run until they run `npm run engine:sync` (needs network). Mitigation: the failure message names the exact remediation, the bypass env var exists for deliberate cases, and the docs matrix explains it. Expect a burst of loud failures in the oldest worktrees.
- **Risk — false failure if the pin is rewritten out of the engine's history** (force-push/rebase upstream). Mitigation: the failure message distinguishes "pin commit not present in this clone" from "behind the pin", and the check never fetches.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Adjacent items (pin lag, spurious gitlink staging in releases, pin/tip policy) are separate work items and are *not* folded in here; they are linked below instead.
- **Assumption — dirty `core` is a warning, not a failure.** Composition remains identifiable; the clobber guard belongs to `engine:sync`/`engine:verify`.
- **Risk — test-path coupling.** A shared `globalSetup` that throws turns every suite red at once if the precheck itself is buggy. Mitigation: pure checker with unit tests over fixtures (no dependency on this repo's live `core` state in the tests), a documented bypass env var, and the manual `npm run engine:check` path for diagnosis.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX** — "Engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH" (`intake_complete`): establishes the *pin tracks the dev tip* policy and the mechanical re-pin. This item consumes that pin but does not change it; if the pin is stale, the preflight still passes for a pin-descendant checkout.
- **MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57** — "Release derived-files step commits a spurious core submodule bump…" (`intake_complete`): the *other* direction of submodule drift (gitlink moved by the build during release). Both items concern "the tree you test/build is not the engine you claim"; keep the fixes disjoint.
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** — the build-scripts-decide-the-engine decision that `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` implement; the composition matrix extends its documentation.
- **MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F** (completed) — the historical dev-HEAD pin/pointer mismatch (`engine-pin.json` vs `core` gitlink); the closest prior instance of "the recorded engine and the composed engine disagree".
- **MS-0MVJPV0BV000LSLW** — precedent for the fast, offline, remediation-printing pre-check pattern (`check-playwright-chromium.ts`).
- **MS-0MVK37SK5009M0NG** (completed) — the project-coverage guard; its H3 hypothesis "stale `core` submodule state" is the same hazard this item makes explicit.
- Docs: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`, `docs/dev/testing.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `README.md`; code: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`.

A machine-generated "Related work (automated report)" section is appended to this description by the `find-related` skill (top matches, ranked by keyword overlap); it is regenerated on every run and is not hand-edited.

## Plan review record

Planning was **decomposed-skip** (effort Small / risk Low, per `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`): the item is one
deliverable and is implemented directly, so no child work items were created. The six automated review stages ran over
the existing content.

| 1. Requirements & AC alignment | Each of AC1–AC6 traced to the Desired change / Users / Constraints sections | AC1 gained the documented bypass env var and the "wiring survives re-scaffold" clause (both were only in Desired change / Risks, so the ACs understated them). AC2 reworded to "at most one identical line per process" because every Vitest project `extends: true` and may each trigger the global setup. |

Completeness | Required fields, `**Key Files:**` syntax (`validate_key_files_format` → no issues) and accuracy vs the real tree | Added the missing drift-guard test to Key Files; added a **Reuse** note (`readPin` / `submoduleIsDirty` are already exported by `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`); recorded that `vite.config.ts` is auto-generated by the engine-owned scaffold, so the change is a surgical addition + guard, not a template edit. |

Acceptance & testability | Every AC pass/fail and drivable from the test suite | All ACs are now testable: pure checker over temp-git fixtures, injected logger for the identity line, drift guard for wiring. The one non-automated clause ("manual stale-worktree reproduction", AC1) is kept as a manual confirmation step. |

# Per-turn loan repayment in the closing sequence

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the loan model slice.

## Goal

As a player holding a loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins leave my wallet at the end of
every turn for `termTurns` turns, the deduction shows up in the turn's net summary as an
expense, and the loan then disappears.

## Context

- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): income,
  staff/community/business ongoing costs, then the incident, then `appendTurnNetRow`.
  Repayment belongs in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Turn net rows are written by `appendTurnNetRow` (delta summary + totals lines) and the
  `TurnResult` carries an optional `turnLedger` (MS-0MVP45KZV006TMUK) with one-off deltas —
  prefer extending that ledger so the Turn Summary dialog can surface the expense rather
  than adding a parallel channel.
- Competitive seats keep their wallet in `state.players[].coins` with
  `state.resourceBank` as the working mirror (`bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`); single-player has no `state.players`. Repayment must work for
  whichever wallet is active, and must not disturb the other seats in a competitive close.
- Producer Q6=A: repayment is deducted unconditionally — a shortfall leaves `coins < 0` and
  the ordinary bankruptcy path decides what happens next. The bailout offer itself is the

## Headline

The Park (`cs-park`) is the **only community space that yields no reputation per
turn**, while carrying the **highest running cost in the game** (40 coins/turn)
— it produces neither income nor reputation and the balance analysis records it
as a net drain. Give it the producer-confirmed **+20 reputation/turn**, keeping
its cost 150 and 40/turn running cost unchanged, restoring it as an attractive
tier-1 Entertainment anchor and the cheapest reputation entry in the game.

## Problem statement

The Park currently provides no value to the player. All seven other community
spaces generate `reputationPerTurn` (Playground 20, Garden 40, Fountain 40,
Library 40, Health Kiosk 60, Shelter 60, Public Art 80); the Park has an empty
`reputationPerTurn` (0) while costing 40 coins/turn to run — the highest
`ongoingCost` of any community space. `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md`
records it as a "pure net drain" (remedied by re-pricing 300 → 150 in
MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5, but the zero reputation remained). The producer decision
(2026-10-28) sets **+20 reputation/turn** with pricing kept at 150/40.

## Users

- **Player** — building an Entertainment cluster should feel rewarded: the Park
  is a tier-1, tutorial-visible card that currently reads as a money pit.
  *"As a player, I want the Park to grow my reputation, so that placing it is a
  strategic choice rather than an obvious mistake."*
- **Producer / balance owner** — confirmed the value and pricing on
  2026-10-28; wants the guardrails verified and the docs updated to match.
- **Developer** — a single-row, data-only change: the machinery that applies
  `reputationPerTurn` (per-turn income, tooltips, AI scoring) already exists and
  needs no engine changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-park` in `src/card-data.csv` gains `reputationPerTurn = 20`
   (producer-confirmed 2026-10-28; integer, no cost or `ongoingCost` change —
   remains 150 and 40). The description is updated with the existing wording
   convention used by Library/Garden/Fountain ("Provides +20 reputation per
   turn."), and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
2. **Value visible automatically** — the Park's card tooltip shows the +20
   rep/turn line, the per-turn reputation total includes it (existing
   `MainStreetEngineCommands` path), and UI/AI scoring that reads
   `reputationPerTurn` reflect the new value with no engine change.
3. **Retune-contract baseline updated deliberately** —
   `tests/main-street/reputation-retune-contract.test.ts` pins `cs-park: 0`
   (`PRE_RETUNE_COMMUNITY_SPACE_REP`). This is the only card whose value
   changes outside the ×4 retune (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE), so the baseline entry
   and the test's rationale comment are updated with a pointer to this item
   (a deliberate, documented contract change, not a silent regression).
4. **Balance sanity** — the Monte Carlo / tutorial guardrails remain within
   band after the change (Park now contributes +20 passive reputation and looks
   more attractive to the AI's community-space scoring); any drift is measured
   and reported, and no band is silently widened.
5. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (Park row and its
   rationale line about "zero reputation and negative net value"),
   `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` (community-space table), and
   any other doc listing Park's rep/turn (e.g.

# tce-main-street dev builds re-pin the engine on every build, invalidating the test cache and pushing the full suite past timeoutPerCommand

Discovered during MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG (child MS-0MVPY2X7L001DW7J), while running the mandated build -> test -> commit order for an evidence-only (no-source-change) child.

```
discovered-from:MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG
```

## Observed

1. `npm run build` runs `npm run engine:sync` first, which does
   `git submodule update --remote core`, moves `./core` to the engine's
   tracked-branch tip, rewrites `configs/engine-pin.json`, and **stages both**
   (`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`, `stageEngineState`).
2. The committed pin (`0409c1eb`) lagged the engine tip (`19f30ac7`) at the
   time, so *every* dev build in *every* worktree produced a dirty tree:

   ```
   M  configs/engine-pin.json
   M  core
   ```
3. The test cache key is `HEAD` plus a content hash of every dirty path
   (submodules hash their own HEAD/status — `skill/test_cache.py:compute_git_state`).
   A pre-warmed green entry recorded on a **clean** tree therefore never matches
   the **dirty** tree the finish gate evaluates, so the finish gate always
   re-runs the full suite instead of consuming the cache.
4. On the shared host the full suite took **2846 s** (measured,
   `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-full.log`, `success: true`) — far above
   `timeoutPerCommand: 1800` in `.pi/test-config.json`. The finish gate then
   died with `Test run 1/3 failed (unknown)`, `failures: []` (*no parsed
   failures — a timeout kill, not a test failure*), and `implement.py finish`
   reported failure for a child with **no source change at all**
   (`/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log`).

## Why it matters

- Any item whose worktree's committed pin lags the engine tip cannot pass
  `implement.py finish` on a loaded host, even with a green full suite, because
  the build re-dirties the tree immediately before the gate.
- The failure surfaces as *"No structured test failures were parsed"*, which
  reads like a flake and invites blind retries.
- It also silently loads an unrelated engine bump into a documentation/evidence
  only commit.

## Candidate remedies (not decided — needs producer triage)

- **A** — the finish gate should not leave build-time re-pins staged when the
  item has no source change; or the cache key should exclude the engine
  gitlink/pin pair (build-artefact churn, not item content).
- **B** — raise `timeoutPerCommand` to cover the measured loaded-host full-suite
  time with headroom (the documented remedy in the implement skill: "Set the
  value high enough to cover the full suite with headroom").
- **C** — make `engine:sync` a no-op when the pin is behind only by engine
  commits unrelated to the item (bump the pin in its own item, not as a side
  effect of every build).

## Acceptance criteria (TBD — needs producer triage)

- [ ] A dev build in a worktree whose pin lags the engine tip either (a) leaves
      no build-artefact dirt in the test cache key, or (b) the finish gate still
      consumes a green cached suite entry.
- [ ] A timeout kill is distinguishable from a real failure in
      `implement.py finish` output (not `unknown` / `failures: []`).
- [ ] Reproduced and pinned by a test at the module under change.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A missing, invalid, non-pinned-key or malformed manifest makes **every** path from that source resolve `null`, logs exactly one source-level warning, and never throws.
- [ ] The remote source never throws for any input (invalid config, non-string path, empty path, throwing transport), asserted by a table-driven test.
- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).
- [ ] No new entry is added to `package.json` dependencies.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, composition
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — boot wiring on the browser path
- `./env.d.ts` — declared env vars
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

## Deliverables

- The end-to-end discovery path: configured URL → verified manifest → served
  CSV → merged pool → listing.
- The configuration, verifier and fetch primitives the later slices harden.
- Signed-manifest fixtures (keypair generation, signing, tampering, fake
  transport) reused by the verification items.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.
